title: Work Mechanics: Reversible vs Irreversible Isothermal & Adiabatic Processes
topics: Reversible Isothermal Work Formula (w = -2.303 nRT log(V₂/V₁))
Adiabatic Reversible Law (PV^γ = const, w = n C_v ΔT)

quickSummary: Work is defined by w = -∫ P_ext dV. Maximum expansion work is produced in a reversible isothermal process (|w_rev| > |w_irr|). In free expansion into a vacuum (P_ext = 0), w = 0, q = 0, and ΔT = 0 for an ideal gas.
summary: Master reversible and irreversible work calculations, adiabatic Poisson relations, and vacuum free expansion.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Reversible vs Irreversible Work Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Reversible vs Irreversible Work Mechanics

summaryBox.title: Work Calculations
summaryBox.takeaway: w = -∫ P_ext dV. For expansion: |w_rev| > |w_irr|. Reversible isothermal: w = -2.303 nRT log₁₀(V₂/V₁).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
REVERSIBLE vs IRREVERSIBLE EXPANSION WORK
                     
   Reversible Isothermal (|w_rev|) > Irreversible Isothermal (|w_irr|)
   
   Reversible:    w_rev = -2.303 nRT log₁₀(V₂ / V₁) = -2.303 nRT log₁₀(P₁ / P₂)
   Irreversible:  w_irr = -P_ext (V₂ - V₁) = -P_ext nRT (1/P₂ - 1/P₁)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• In a **Reversible Process**, the driving force differs infinitesimally from opposing force ($P_{\text{ext}} = P_{\text{int}} \pm dP$), maintaining quasi-static equilibrium and extracting maximum work from the system.
• In an **Irreversible Process**, expansion occurs against a constant external pressure $P_{\text{ext}}$, yielding less work ($|w_{\text{rev}}| > |w_{\text{irr}}|$).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 Adiabatic Expansion & Free Expansion
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 Adiabatic Expansion & Free Expansion
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Reversible Adiabatic Expansion ($q = 0 \implies \Delta U = w$)**:
$$\mathbf{P V^\gamma = \text{Constant} \quad \vert \quad T V^{\gamma-1} = \text{Constant} \quad \vert \quad T^\gamma P^{1-\gamma} = \text{Constant}}$$
$$\mathbf{w_{\text{rev, ad}} = n C_{v,m} (T_2 - T_1) = \frac{P_2 V_2 - P_1 V_1}{\gamma - 1} = \frac{nR (T_2 - T_1)}{\gamma - 1}}$$
*(Note: Adiabatic expansion always causes cooling: $T_2 < T_1$)*.

2. **Free Expansion into Vacuum ($P_{\text{ext}} = 0$)**:
$$\mathbf{w = 0 \quad \text{for any free expansion!}}$$
For an Ideal Gas: $w = 0, q = 0 \implies \Delta U = 0 \implies \mathbf{\Delta T = 0, \Delta H = 0}$.

quickRevision: Adiabatic: T V^(γ-1) = const; expansion causes cooling (T₂ < T₁).
Free expansion into vacuum: w = 0, q = 0, ΔU = 0, ΔT = 0.
keyFormulae: w_ad = n C_v (T₂ - T₁) = nR(T₂ - T₁) / (γ - 1)
